text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. presidential emissary for Cyprus, Richard Holbrooke, expected to intervene on Cyprus problem in March 1998.

- Turkish Cypriot murdered in broad daylight in Limassol on Saturday may have been gunned down by agent of Turkish MIT secret service; Turkish Cypriot was detained in the past on suspicion of spying on Greek Cypriot army positions.
- Communist Akel calls for in-depth debate on Turkish threats to integrate occupied areas with Turkey.
- U.N. mediator for Cyprus, Diego Cordovez, due to submit report to Security Council on Wednesday on latest round of talks at Glion in Switzerland.

- International mediators want to keep impetus on efforts to solve Cyprus dispute to avoid falling into new impasse. U.N.'s priority is meeting between President Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Denktash in Nicosia in September to discuss humanitarian issues.
- Turkish secret service MIT murdered one of its own agents, a Turkish Cypriot living in Limassol who had been arrested in past on suspicion of spying but later released.
